notes: Governing documents: the AAUP-WSU TET collective bargaining agreement (2014-2017) covers 'all full-time tenured and tenure-track faculty' (2.3) and takes precedence over inconsistent policies (1.3). Its stated term ended 2017-06-30; the version note records that the successor took effect 2019-02-01, so it is read as in force on 2018-02-26. University Policy 8430 (Leaves of Absence) also covers 'all faculty'. So a governing document for TET faculty leave is saved: missing is false (the rule for records with no governing document does not apply).

Main-campus tenure-stream member's provisions: FMLA 12 workweeks (c1), drawn first from accrued sick and vacation leave (c2, own balance, 0 paid weeks under R1); unpaid child care leave for the rest of the semester plus the following semester after FMLA (c4, guaranteed); unpaid disability leave for the birth parent once sick leave is exhausted (c3, discretionary, up to 6 months, to 1 year); paid Parental Teaching Relief for a primary caretaker, one semester of no teaching or two semesters at 50% (c5/c6, in_lieu_of, guaranteed on request); one-year tenure-clock extension (c7, discretionary). No employer-paid parental or childbirth leave exists for TET faculty.

Other groups: the paid Parental Leave on the HR page (c17: birth mothers 6 weeks, others 3 weeks) covers 'eligible university staff' and is found only on that summary page (summary_only). Policy 2080 (c18-c22) covers non-bargaining faculty (lecturers, clinical faculty, instructors), not TET faculty; it is written for the old quarter calendar.

Birth parent chain: FMLA 12 workweeks from the birth (sick leave pay within it) -> child care leave for the remainder of the current semester and the following semester (1 to 2 semesters, consecutive_after FMLA). Disability leave (after sick leave is exhausted) is placed after the sick-leave component and is not linked to the child care leave. Teaching relief (one semester, or 50% over two) is an alternative pair, unlinked to the leaves (it must start within a year of the birth).

Non-birth parent chain: FMLA 12 workweeks from the birth -> child care leave (1 to 2 semesters, consecutive_after FMLA); the 30.3.2 text names only a 'male' member ('Biological Father'). Teaching relief as for the birth parent, for a primary caretaker.
Calendar: CBA 9.1 states fifteen-week semesters (also 7.7.1 and the 2015 sick-days MOU); term_weeks 15.

Documents cited but not saved: the Faculty Handbook faculty workload policy (CBA 19.1); the HR site pages for Short Term Disability, Long Term Disability, Family and Medical Leave, Adoption Assistance Plan and Sick Leave (HR page navigation; the Short Term Disability page may describe a plan, for which group unknown); the governing staff parental leave policy behind the HR page; the University Equal Educational and Employment Opportunity Policies (CBA 4.3); department bylaws; the 'summary of the Family and Medical Leave Act' and FMLA forms (Policy 8430); the 2014-2017 NTE agreement; the August 5, 2015 MOU is saved (2018_07, not parental).

Not components: professional development leave and special fellowship leave (CBA Art. 29; 2018_07 MOU; Policy 8430.4), court leave, military leave, bereavement use of sick leave, and the vacation article (fiscal-year faculty only): none can be used for a birth or adoption, or (vacation) it applies only to fiscal-year appointees and is noted with sick leave use under FMLA (30.2.3). CBA 11.2.9 (evaluation not penalised for sick leave) and 31.6.5 (a list pointing to provisions already coded) add no provision.

The documents do not state whether TET faculty can receive the staff paid Parental Leave, or any short-term disability plan for faculty; no employer pay during the child care or disability leave is stated.
